subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification - shared vs dedicated (FinPay)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 23:15:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment mode qualification - FinPay call follow-up

Hi Jordan / Samira -

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups to help us recommend the best deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary workload: low-latency payment scoring + enrichment for customer UX (in-path calls).
- Estimated steady traffic: ~150-250 requests/sec (peaks ~400 rps)
- Token volume: ~80k-120k tokens/day, with bursts during batch jobs
- Latency target: P95 <= 250ms for in-path calls; occasional higher latency OK for async jobs
- Data controls: PCI-adjacent, want audit logs and key management; will need to confirm exact flow with security team

Key qualification questions so we can be prescriptive:
1) How strict do you need instance-level isolation? Is noisy-neighbor avoidance a hard requirement or a risk you can tolerate with mitigation (e.g., KV / prefix caching + routing)?
2) Any hard SLOs/SLA numbers from your side (uptime, latency at percentile)?
3) Do you expect throughput growth >2x over the next 12 months?
4) Are there procurement or legal constraints that push you to Private (VPC/on-prem) vs Dedicated?

Next steps I propose:
- If isolation is a hard requirement, we should prioritize Dedicated capacity or Private VPC. I can share a short note on our isolation guarantees and typical SLOs.
- If fine with shared infra but need latency assurances, we can look at a hybrid: Dedicated for in-path, Hosted for async/batch.
- Share traffic sample (CSV) and any SLO doc you have; I’ll loop in our infra lead (Priyom) for technical deep-dive.

Attachments: I attached a short traffic-sample template you can fill - helps route sizing.

Would you be available for a 30-45 minute technical deep-dive next week? I can bring Priyom and Marissa to go into isolation, autoscaling, and SLA specifics.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks, Vivek - great notes and thanks for the template. A few answers from our side: 

- Isolation: we are pretty sensitive. Noisy neighbor incidents in our current environment have caused P95 latency spikes that impacted UX. For the initial rollout (customer-facing scoring), we prefer dedicated isolation.
- SLOs: our product team needs P95 <= 250ms and P99 <= 600ms for in-path calls, with 99.9% availability.
- Growth: we expect traffic to double in 6-9 months as we expand to two new regions.
- Procurement: we have some procurement checks for on-prem but prefer cloud first; if Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool) meets our isolation and SLA needs cost-effectively, that is ideal. Private VPC would be considered if there are unresolved security questions.

I attached a short internal note with current request volumes by endpoint and rough token sizes. Happy to share any additional telemetry you need.

Can do a deep-dive next Tue/Wed afternoon ET.
—Jordan

jmills@finpay.com | +1 646-555-0199

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification - FinPay call follow-up

Jordan - great, thanks for the clear answers. That helps a lot. A few clarifications and what we’ll bring to the deep-dive: 

1) Isolation options and tradeoffs:
   - Hosted (shared): lowest friction / cost. We rely on workload-aware batching, prefix/KV caching, and prioritized routing to meet latency targets, but there is inherent shared tenancy risk. Not recommended for strict isolation needs.
   - Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools reserved for your account. Provides strong noisy-neighbor isolation (per-tenant queues + reserved CPU/GPU). We can offer latency SLOs for P95; exact numbers vary by commitment level.
   - Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation + customer-managed infra; for regulated workloads where control-plane separation or additional compliance controls are required.

2) SLOs & guarantees:
   - For Dedicated we typically commit to P95 latency targets and 99.9% availability in our SLA; we’ll scope the exact P95 number to your workload (model selection, sequence length, and concurrency affect tokens/sec).
   - We’ll include KV-prefix caching, sticky routing, and reserved capacity buffers for in-path endpoints to reduce tail risk.

3) Cost & sizing: Priyom will size the Dedicated pool based on the CSV you provided and expected growth. We’ll show a comparison: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with 6-12 month TCO.

Attached: preliminary SLA draft and a short isolation explainer (SLA-draft-FinPay.pdf).

Next steps:
- Priyom to review your traffic sample and come to the technical deep-dive with a recommended Dedicated configuration.
- Schedule deep-dive: Tue 16 Mar 2027, 14:00-14:45 ET (we’ll send calendar invite).
- After deep-dive, we can share a formal Dedicated pricing estimate and an SLA addendum for procurement review.

I’ll send a calendar invite and include a tech doc link for our isolation patterns.

Best,
Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
